claim: In the same model at volume fraction 0.66, the skewness and excess kurtosis of the distribution of shear-stress magnitudes change more sharply across the glass-fluid transition than the mean stress does: in the fluid the magnitude is effectively half-normal (skewness about 0.995, excess kurtosis about 0.869), in the glass the skewness is near zero and the excess kurtosis negative, and a contour at 0.5 in either marks the transition.
validity_conditions: A MODEL RESULT. Dry three-dimensional mixture of soft repulsive spheres (a harmonic repulsion approximated by a Morse form), half small and half large (radius ratio sqrt(2)) in both the active and the passive population; active particles are overdamped active Brownian particles, passive ones have no propulsion; kT = 1e-4, Dr = 3 Dt/a0^2 with a0 the small diameter; steady shear with Lees-Edwards boundaries; Euler-Maruyama at time step 1e-2 in HOOMD-blue (version not stated); total strain 10 with the first 5 discarded; no hydrodynamics, no walls, no friction. Peclet number v0/(a0 Dr), which is peclet_number_steric with the small diameter as the length. Shear rates in model units from 1e-6 to 1e-2. Volume fractions (three dimensions) from 0.60 to 0.72. Shown at volume fraction 0.66 and the lowest shear rate, 1e-6 in model units. A method the paper offers as an additional and probably better criterion than the mean stress; the half-normal values follow from uncorrelated collisions in a flowing fluid.
